record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: Is there a valid theoretical and experimental account of mind-matter interaction, especially one that explains reported effects of language, music, or intention on water structure, clarifies any relation to cymatics, and yields new testable predictions about the hidden structure of water?

evidence.quote: Questions: - Is there a valid theoretical relation to describe the Mind-Matter interaction in the context of quantum physics?
- Are there new observations predicted by the Mind-Matter interaction paradigm, in particular concerning the hidden structure of water?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Formulate, within the framework of quantum physics, a theoretical model of "mind–matter interaction" that simultaneously: (i) provides a quantitative account of reported experimental claims that human intention, spoken or written language, or music can influence the microscopic or mesoscopic structure of liquid water; (ii) clarifies whether and how such effects are related to cymatics (the study of visible patterns produced in fluids or granular media by sound vibrations), making the relation precise in mathematical terms; and (iii) yields concrete, falsifiable predictions about hidden structural features of water (for instance, metastable coherent domains, long-range correlations, or other order parameters) that go beyond standard molecular dynamics descriptions. Provide both the theoretical formulation and a corresponding experimental protocol whose outcomes would decide the validity of the model.
artifact.status_search_result: The question lies outside mainstream physics and mathematics; no peer-reviewed theoretical-experimental framework establishing mind–matter interaction or its purported effects on water structure is accepted in the scientific literature. Related claims (e.g., Emoto-style water memory) have been widely criticized and not reproduced under controlled conditions, so the posed problem remains unresolved/open in the sense that no validated account exists.

status_evidence.title: Water memory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Water memory is the purported ability of water to retain a memory of substances previously dissolved in it... The concept is not consistent with the accepted scientific understanding of physical chemistry.
status_evidence.claim: No accepted scientific framework supports memory-like structural effects in water.
